2424.full: ἐκούσιος, -ον (έκών), [in LXX chiefly for נְדָבָה, as Num.15:3 (κατ᾽ ἑ) ;] usually of actions, voluntary: κατὰ ἑ., of free will (Lft., in l), Phm 14.† (AS)

2432.full: ὑπο-τίθημι [in LXX for שׂוּם, etc. ;] to place under, lay down. Metaphorical, τ. τράχηλον ὑποθεῖναι, to risk one's life (see Deiss., LAE, 119 f.): Rom.16:4; mid., to suggest: 1Ti.4:6.† (AS)

2433.full: 1. to weave , ἱστὸν ὑφαίνειν to weave a web, (Homer); ἱμάτιον (Plato Philosophus), etc.:—;absolute to weave, ply the loom , (Herdotus Historicus):—;Mid., ἱμάτιον ὑφαίνεσθαι to weave oneself a cloak, (Plato Philosophus) 2. to contrive, plan, invent , Lat. texere, δόλον ὑφαίνειν (Iliad by Homer); μῆτιν ὑφ. (Odyssey by Homer) 3. generally, to create, construct , (Pindar) (ML)

2442.full: 1. opposite to ψιλός in all senses: 2. thick with hair, hairy, shaggy, rough , (Odyssey by Homer); of young hares, downy , (Herdotus Historicus) 3. thick with leaves , (Odyssey by Homer); θρίδαξ δασέα a lettuce with all the leaves on, (Herdotus Historicus):—;of places, thick with bushes or wood , (Odyssey by Homer); διὰ τῶν δασέων through the copses , (Aristophanes Comicus); δ. ὕληι thick with copse-wood, (Herdotus Historicus), etc.; rarely with genitive, δασὺς δένδρων (Xenophon Historicus):—; τὸ δασύ bushy country , (Xenophon Historicus) (ML)
